caption:
What can you tell about a clinic before anyone speaks to you?
More than you would think, and most of it is near the floor.

Indoor slippers at the door mean they expect you to be here a while, not to drop in. A blanket folded on the chair means someone has thought about the fact that treatment rooms run cold. A paper bag handed over on the way out means aftercare is supposed to follow you home rather than end at reception.

None of it is decoration. All of it is an assumption the clinic has made about what is going to happen to you.

This is an observation, not a research finding, and it is not a way to rank anywhere. Plenty of good rooms are completely plain. What it gives you is something to read while you wait, instead of the wall.

Three more worth noticing. Whether the consultation happens at a desk in the open or in a room with a door. What is on the wall - certificates, machines, or neither. And who greets you, and whether that same person is in the room later.

None of this decides anything. All of it is information.

General education only.

#KoreanClinic #PatientExperience #MedicalTourism #MedicalAesthetics #KoreanAesthetics
first_comment: The slippers are the one nobody mentions and the one that tells you the most - they only exist if the clinic expects you to stay. What is the strangest thing you have seen in a waiting room?
